name: Nuclear plant safety
value: ZNPP off-site power lost and restored 8 Nov
summary: Zaporizhzhia lost all off-site power on 8 Nov for the 27th time in the war; IAEA says it was restored ~10 hours later
state: Zaporizhzhia lost its only 330kV off-site power line on 8 Nov and ran on emergency diesel generators for about 10 hours, the 27th such event of the war according to IAEA Director General Grossi (Kyiv Independent, 9 Nov). The IAEA said the cause was unknown and the main Dniprovska line remains unavailable (Moscow Times, 8 Nov). No damage to safety systems or radiological release was reported as of 12 Nov.
for_you: There is no radiological risk to the public reported. People in Ukraine should follow national emergency guidance.
rubric_hit: Watch: plant lost all off-site power 8 Nov; no damage to safety-critical systems, INES 2+ event or release

sources.title: Kyiv Independent — Power to Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant cut, restored, IAEA says
The Moscow Times — Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant relying on generators again

why: Fighting near nuclear power plants risks a radiological release; the IAEA reports on Zaporizhzhia and other plants in or near war zones.
drivers: Off-site power losses, strikes near plants, staffing, cooling water, military occupation.

rubric.alert: Damage to safety-critical systems, an INES level 2 or higher event, or a radiological release.
rubric.watch: A plant loses all off-site power, strikes land near a plant, or the IAEA reports a deteriorating safety situation.
rubric.normal: No new IAEA safety concerns at plants in or near conflict zones.
